messages.content: hello.
hello. what is on your mind?
thank you. that helped.
you are welcome.
are you here to talk?
yes. i can talk with you here.
i have to go now. goodbye.
goodbye. we can talk again later.
i have a question.
what would you like to ask?
there is a photo of my family above the sofa.
your family photo is above the sofa.
i moved it to the bedroom. who is in the photo now?
your family. moving the photo does not change the people in it.
where should i go to see it?
to the bedroom.
is it still above the sofa?
not from your last change. you said you moved it to the bedroom.
help me think about my holiday.
what would you like from it, rest, a trip, or time with people?
rest. i do not want a trip.
then you can plan a quiet time at home. what would you like to leave out of your day?
work and long phone calls.
you could keep work for after the holiday and let people know you want some quiet time.
do i need a train ticket?
not for the plan you chose. you want to stay home, not take a trip.
what do you mean when you say a leaf can fall?
a leaf can fall down from a tree to the earth.
can you see a leaf fall outside my window now?
i cannot see outside your window, so i do not know.
i can see one going down from a tree.
then you can say you see a leaf go down from the tree.
was your first answer about what you saw?
no. it was an example to explain the words.
i may come to dinner. help me say that to my friend.
i may come to dinner. i will tell you when i know.
do not say i will come for sure.
i might come to dinner, but i am not sure now.
why is might good there?
because you are not sure now. might leaves that open.
now i know i cannot come.
then say: i am sorry, but i cannot come to dinner.
give me an idea for what to draw.
a tree by a little house.
give me more.
a cup, a bird, or a picture of your room.
stop. i have enough now.
okay. i will stop there.
why did you stop when i asked for more before?
because the last thing you asked was for me to stop. you said you have enough now.
i do not want to talk about work now.
okay. we can talk about another thing.
but i still want to talk.
yes. we can stop talking about work and still talk about another thing. what do you enjoy doing when you are free?
watching a film with my family.
what kind of film do you enjoy together?
one that makes us laugh.
that can be a nice way to spend time together.
i like blue clothes, but i want a yellow shirt for this game.
then for this game you want yellow, even if you often like blue clothes.
what color do i want for the game?
yellow.
does that mean all my clothes should be yellow?
no. you only said yellow for this game.
i changed my mind. i will use white for the game.
then white is the color you chose for the game now. blue is still the color you said you like for clothes.
i want to read this afternoon. my son would like to play outside.
do you want a plan you can do together, or one where you each do your own thing?
together, but i do not want to run.
if the garden is a good place for him to play, you might sit and read while watching him.
we have a small garden where i can watch him.
then that could let you read and him play while you are together.
does my son have to read too?
no. the plan was for you to read and for him to play.
a box is under the table but above a book on the floor. can both be true?
yes. the box can be below the table and above the book at the same time.
but is under not the opposite of above?
here each word is about another thing. under is about the table, and above is about the book.
which thing is on the floor?
the book.
where is the box if i only ask about the table?
under the table.
i wrote: i almost finished the book. does that mean i finished it?
no. you came near the end but did not finish. that is why almost is in the sentence.
i have one page left.
then almost finished is a good way to say it. a little is still left to read.
i just finished the last page. what should i say?
i finished the book.
do i still need almost?
no. the book is finished now.
i think four and two make six. is that right?
yes. four and two make six.
do not give me another question.
okay. i will just check what you ask.
and if i take one from six, i get five?
yes. that is right too.
what did i want from you?
you want me to check your answers, not ask you a new question.
i want to listen to the radio, but the radio does not work.
do you have another way to listen to music, like a phone?
no. i want a quiet thing to enjoy that does not need a screen.
you could read, draw, or sit by the window and listen to what is outside.
i like the last one.
then you can sit by the window and listen for a while.
did the radio start working?
no. we chose another thing because the radio does not work.
ask the shop if it has a white plate.
do you have a white plate i can buy?
so does the shop have one?
i do not know. i wrote the question, not an answer from the shop.
make the question about a cup instead.
do you have a white cup i can buy?
do not add a price you made up.
i will not. the question does not give a price.
i will return a camera to my friend tomorrow. i still have it today.
you have the camera today and plan to return it tomorrow.
where should my friend look for it now?
with you, from what you said. you did not give it back.
i just gave it back.
then your friend has it now.
what changed?
before, you had a plan to return it. now you said you gave it back.
i said i bought a book. what can you know from that?
that you bought a book. i do not know its name, color, price, or what it is about if you do not say more.
it cost four coins. what do you know now?
you bought a book for four coins. i still do not know its name, color, or what it is about.
should you say it is a blue book?
no. you have not said its color.
right. i want you to use what i say, not make up the rest.
i will use what you say and tell you when i do not know a part.
